title: Render evidence on demand; stop writing HTML at task finish
context: System was generating and writing HTML evidence files whenever tasks completed, creating I/O and storage overhead. Touches invariant(s): con_039cee7367 (Memory hygiene is the agent's job, done without waiting for the human: accept shipped roadmap proposals, settle provenance-repair escalations (apply the true commit or drop), re-anchor or stale findings, and land the resulting capture commits through a PR. Only decisions that need genuine product judgment are queued for the human.); con_8460b6770f (Config/provider writers must merge idempotently into existing user files and refuse to clobber an unparseable file); con_91e6074b66 (Capability pages for functionality shipped in the current release must state that it ships today and must not retain the stale banner 'In development for the next release.'); con_e04226bd05 (The MCP server must stay client-agnostic: all assistants point to the same .hunch/ graph; no Claude-only behavior in the server).
decision: Evidence view generation deferred to on-demand invocation. Stop hook and MCP finish no longer write files; instead, card's Evidence line names the CLI command (hunch report <id> --html). Graph record remains durable source; rendering happens when user asks via CLI or VS Code view.
consequences: Eliminated I/O write on every task completion
Graph record is single source of truth; HTML is derived view
Evidence view generated lazily when CLI or UI invokes it
Updated all documentation and integration points (copilot, windsurf, claude.md rules)
Removed node:url dependency (likely from HTML generation path)
alternatives_rejected: Keep eager HTML generation at task completion
Embed rendered HTML in graph record
Store evidence as static files per task
